As for what you could do to overcome it, if it's not the kind of loneliness I experience, then meet people etc. If you have problems with confidence, consider checking out Asperger's or social anxiety forums (even if you have neither of these - I have experience with both - it still might be helpful to check out how they try to cope with their social-related issues).

If it is the kind I experience, then think about some kind of mental health check-up. If you can't afford the treatment (if it costs where you are), then look into any kind of charities that could support you in your area. There are online CBT courses as well, which could hopefully help deal with any hurtful thoughts you are having.

Scenario (1) Shot by quickdraw:
This is an extremely difficult situation to protect yourself against. It went from about a 3 to a 10 in half a second. The officer had just approached: the best one could hope for is to call the individual away from the car. Even then, you're still not really protected from a quick draw scenario until you've verified the individual isn't armed. That would, of course, require a pat-down. You don't shoot someone for being shifty, but you can't protect yourself from a quick-draw scenario.

Scenario (2) An aggressive individual goes from a shoving match to pacing down the officer.
The guy takes 10 steps towards an officer, around 5 of which were within swinging distance of the officer. Those same 5 were also at an officer that had his gun drawn and fixed on him. It would be difficult to drum up controversy around this scenario, so why bother highlighting it? Ideally you'd use a taser, though, since it's not clear he's armed and hasn't actually taken a swing at the officer yet.

Scenario (3) a man semi-restrained on the ground.
This guy doesn't pose a huge threat anymore, he's already partially restrained. He's uncooperative, but you don't shoot someone for being uncooperative. Also not a difficult situation to decide to shoot or not.
